subject: Pittsburgh benched its quarterback for talking
summary: The Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers over his radio criticism, tariffs go from leak to proposal, Starlink offers to skip federal money, and a pope's private diary goes public.

lead.head: A vote of confidence lasted one day
text: The Steelers made a quarterback decision in public and in a hurry. Aaron Rodgers was benched a day after the team publicly backed him, and the team is reported to be moving to release him after he criticised coach McCarthy on a radio show.

The order of events is the story. A vote of confidence, a radio appearance, a benching. Teams can live with a struggling quarterback. They have a harder time living with one who argues with the coach in front of an audience. The team's own account and the reporters who broke the news agree on the outline, and the reach on the day shows how many people were waiting for it.

notes.head: The tariff leak became a proposal
notes.text: Tuesday's Wall Street Journal report now has a follow-up. The Trade Representative has proposed new tariffs on a long list of trading partners after its industrial-subsidies investigation, and U.S. stocks fell again on Wednesday. A proposal is still not a rate, so the market is pricing a range, not a number.

notes.head: Starlink offers to skip the grant
notes.text: SpaceX says Starlink would give up its federal rural broadband awards and still serve those locations, with free equipment and a ten-year commitment. States that refuse the new model agreement would have to find other providers. It is a clever offer: it turns a subsidy fight into a question of who else can actually build.

notes.head: A pope's private diary goes public
notes.text: The private diary of Pope Francis, kept from 1992 to 2024 and released after his death, has been published. It describes visions of the devil and a spiritual crisis, and it is the first look at his own account of fear, temptation and power.

text: Three of these stories turn on one question: who gets to set the terms in public. A coach lost an argument he did not start, a trade office is testing the market before it commits, and a company is offering a government a deal on its own terms.
My call is that the Steelers will be judged on how they handle the next quarterback, not on this benching.
